episodes.156126: Isolated afternoon thunderstorms produced small hail and gusty winds across north central and northeast Alabama. Outflow from the thunderstorms knocked down a large tree near Priceville in Morgan County.
episodes.156127: A mid-evening severe thunderstorm moved into some northwest counties and produced very large hail.
episodes.156129: An upper level low pressure system moving through the Great Lakes region resulted in  scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon hours. Some of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.156141: A late afternoon thunderstorm produced some hail.
episodes.156635: A strong upper trough dove southeast across the Northern and Central Plains on April 9th, reinforcing a cold front southeast into the Southern Plains. The approach of this storm system enhanced a southerly low level jet, which allowed for the return of a warm front north across East Texas, North Louisiana, Southern Arkansas, and extreme Southeast Oklahoma, resulting in very warm, humid, and unstable air in advance of the front. The combination of this increasing instability, wind shear, and strong forcing ahead of the cold front and associated upper level storm system resulted in a prolonged period of severe thunderstorms across much of the region, with numerous reports of large hail and occasional damaging winds across East Texas. These storms finally diminished during the early morning hours of April 10th with the passage of the cold front.
episodes.156637: A strong upper trough dove southeast across the Northern and Central Plains on April 9th, reinforcing a cold front southeast into the Southern Plains. The approach of this storm system enhanced a southerly low level jet, which allowed for the return of a warm front north across East Texas, North Louisiana, Southern Arkansas, and extreme Southeast Oklahoma, resulting in very warm, humid, and unstable air in advance of the front. The combination of this increasing instability, wind shear, and strong forcing ahead of the cold front and associated upper level storm system resulted in a prolonged period of severe thunderstorms across much of the region, with numerous reports of large hail and occasional damaging winds across Southwest Arkansas. An isolated tornado also touched down across Southern Little River County along a line of severe thunderstorms along the cold front. These storms finally exited Southwest Arkansas during the early morning hours of April 10th with the passage of the cold front.
episodes.156639: A strong upper trough dove southeast across the Northern and Central Plains on April 9th, reinforcing a cold front southeast into the Southern Plains. The approach of this storm system enhanced a southerly low level jet, which allowed for the return of a warm front north across East Texas, North Louisiana, Southern Arkansas, and extreme Southeast Oklahoma, resulting in very warm, humid, and unstable air in advance of the front. The combination of this increasing instability, wind shear, and strong forcing ahead of the cold front and associated upper level storm system resulted in a prolonged period of severe thunderstorms across much of the region, with numerous reports of large hail and occasional damaging winds across North Louisiana. These storms finally exited North Louisiana during the early morning hours of April 10th with the passage of the cold front.
episodes.156808: Scattered thunderstorms produced isolated large hail and strong winds during the afternoon and evening. Semi-discrete convection formed within a broad confluence zone. Surface temperatures exceeded 80 degrees, with surface dewpoints barely reaching 50. A dry boundary layer supported low-level lapse rates exceeding 9 C/km across much of the Ohio Valley. Up to 1000 J/kg of mixed-layer cape and 30-40 kts of effective bulk wind shear supported large hail with the strongest, longest lived updrafts. The dry boundary layer also supported efficient downward momentum transport of some of the stronger downdraft cores.
episodes.156809: Scattered thunderstorms produced isolated large hail up to the size of golf balls, along with isolated wind damage during the afternoon and evening. Between 3:30 and 7:30 PM, approximately 20 reports of hail dime-size or larger hail or wind damage were received. The vast majority of reports were large hail. Semi-discrete convection formed within a broad confluence zone. Surface temperatures exceeded 80 degrees, with surface dewpoints barely reaching 50. A dry boundary layer supported low-level lapse rates exceeding 9 C/km across much of the Ohio Valley. Up to 1000 J/kg of mixed-layer cape and 30-40 kts of effective bulk wind shear supported large hail with the strongest, longest lived updrafts. The dry boundary layer also supported efficient downward momentum transport of some of the stronger downdraft cores.
episodes.156827: A few isolated severe thunderstorms produced hail over portions of the eastern West Virginia panhandle during the mid afternoon hours.
episodes.156880: A small, but strong thunderstorm moved north across western Lincoln County during the early evening hours.  The thunderstorm produced strong winds that knocked a tree down in Cyruston.
episodes.156925: An isolated thunderstorm produced small hail.
episodes.157030: After a cool morning with some showers, clouds began to break and allow weak to moderate instability to build ahead of a weak prefrontal surface trough, located over central Kentucky and Middle Tennessee. Across eastern Kentucky, the most favorable instability and shear environment was observed southwest of KY-15. By mid-afternoon, storms were firing over the Lake Cumberland area and tracking from southwest-to-northeast onto fairly remote portions of the Cumberland Plateau. During the early and mid-evening, the focus for the strongest storms shifted eastward toward Pine and Black mountains before waning with the loss of daytime heating and the passage of a trailing cold front. Many of these storms featured rotating updrafts which produced swaths of small to marginally severe hail. The strongest storms produced up to half dollar size hail in Bell and Clay counties. In Bell County, some roadways were nearly covered by hail.
episodes.157095: Severe thunderstorms developed into eastern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 9th, ahead of a cold front that was moving into the area. The strongest thunderstorms produced hail up to golf ball size and damaging wind gusts through the evening.
episodes.157096: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved northward across northwestern Arkansas during the early afternoon of the 9th, as a warm front moved across the area. The strongest storms produced hail up to nickel size and damaging wind. Another round of thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas during the evening, with the approach of a cold front from the west. The strongest of these storms produced damaging wind across portions of the area.
episodes.157169: Strong to severe storms moved across the state on April 7th and again on April 9th and 10th associated with the passage two cold fronts. Large hail and damaging winds were the main impacts noted.
episodes.157183: Multiple round of showers and thunderstorms ahead of a strong cold front affected the tri-state region during the April 9-10 period.  An initial round of storms on April 9th brought primarily large hail to the region.  The severe activity on April 10th remained just to the south of southeastern Alabama across the Florida panhandle.
episodes.157184: Multiple round of showers and thunderstorms ahead of a strong cold front affected the tri-state region during the April 9-10 period.  An initial round of storms on April 9th brought primarily large hail to the region, and then a squall line pushed through on April 10th with primarily damaging winds as well as a few tornadoes, mainly across Florida.  Some flooding was also reported, mainly across Florida where the heaviest rainfall amounts occurred in a short period of time.
episodes.157235: On the afternoon of April 9th, thunderstorms along the mountains transpired and led to a few instances of hail in Upshur and Pocahontas Counties.
episodes.157274: Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed over the region through the day in a moderately unstable atmosphere across north Georgia. Isolated severe thunderstorms produced a few reports of thunderstorm wind damage in northwest Georgia.
episodes.157634: A strong spring storm system comprising of a pair of upper level disturbances, a dryline, and a cold front generated several instances of severe hail across North Texas. Hail stones up to 3 was recorded.
episodes.157635: Thunderstorms developed across Central Texas as a warm front moved north through the area during the afternoon of April 8th. Large hail and damaging winds accompanied a few of these storms.
episodes.157669: All of Ohio was in the warm sector of an occluded surface low that drifted from far-northern Wisconsin toward western Lake Superior during the late morning through early evening of April 9th. Aloft, a shortwave trough advanced northeastward from southern Lake Michigan and the Mid Ohio Valley toward Lake Erie as the disturbance revolved around a 500 mb low drifting northeastward from northern Wisconsin toward the western Upper Peninsula of Michigan. Ahead of the shortwave trough, scattered rain showers impacted northern Ohio during the early evening. One of these showers managed to generate a downburst in a moderate shear/low CAPE environment.
episodes.157746: Numerous thunderstorms developed along a cold front as it moved across central and eastern OK during the afternoon and evening hours of the 9th. Large to at times very large hail was reported with some of these storms.
episodes.157811: A stalled frontal boundary became the focus of a line of strong to severe thunderstorms across the area. This line was long-lived and produced dozens of reports of wind damage, flash flooding and even multiple house fires caused by lightning.
episodes.157816: A warm front lifted north through the Mid-South during the day on April 9th. As a result, moist and unstable air pushed into the region ahead of a potent upper-level disturbance approaching from the Central Plains. A couple of lines of severe storms with large hail ignited and pushed across Northeast Arkansas and West Tennessee during the early evening hours. Another line developed across North Mississippi and rolled through later in the evening with damaging winds, large hail, and some flash flooding.
episodes.157817: A warm front lifted north through the Mid-South during the day on April 9th. As a result, moist and unstable air pushed into the region ahead of a potent upper-level disturbance approaching from the Central Plains. A couple of lines of severe storms with large hail ignited and pushed across Northeast Arkansas and West Tennessee during the early evening hours. Another line developed across North Mississippi and rolled through later in the evening with damaging winds, large hail, and some flash flooding.
episodes.157818: A warm front lifted north through the Mid-South during the day on April 9th. As a result, moist and unstable air pushed into the region ahead of a potent upper-level disturbance approaching from the Central Plains. A couple of lines of severe storms with large hail ignited and pushed across Northeast Arkansas and West Tennessee during the early evening hours. Another line developed across North Mississippi and rolled through later in the evening with damaging winds, large hail, and some flash flooding.
episodes.157830: The active Spring storm season continued with another round of severe storms Friday night into Saturday. A strong storm system moved across the area. Ahead of this system, a very moist and unstable airmass developed, setting the stage for widespread severe storm development. Very cold temperatures in the mid levels of the atmosphere allowing very large hail to develop, including the largest hail stone ever recorded in Baldwin County. Along with the very large hail, damaging winds were also widespread.
episodes.157883: An isolated thunderstorm produced hail up to quarters in size.
episodes.157889: A storm system that moved from the southern High Plains into the Mid-Mississippi Valley brought widespread rain and strong to severe thunderstorms to locations in Missouri near the Kansas, Oklahoma and Arkansas borders during the afternoon and evening. Sporadic reports of hail larger than quarters and wind damage were received from these locations.
episodes.157896: Warm front lifting north across Virginia in an area of modest instability and shear allowed for several storms to develop that produced mainly hail, with isolated wind damage.
episodes.157917: An airmass characterized by deep shear, steep mid level lapse rates, and above normal daytime temperatures combined to produce favorable conditions for large hail.
episodes.157988: Showers and thunderstorms developed in association with a frontal system moving through the region. Some of these storms produced hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.157989: Showers and thunderstorms developed in association with a frontal system moving through the region. Some of these storms produced hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.157990: Showers and thunderstorms developed in association with a frontal system moving through the region. Some of these storms produced a few tornadoes, hail, and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.158028: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a warm front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of south central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.158030: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a warm front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.158053: An upper level area of low pressure passing through the region with modest instability and ample shear, coupled with early season low freezing levels produced multiple long tracked hail storms throughout much of southern Virginia.
episodes.158055: An upper level areas of low pressure passing through the region with modest instability and ample shear, coupled with early season low freezing levels produced several large hail producing thunderstorms.
episodes.158143: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a warm front produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.158190: A warm front draped across the region helped trigger scattered to numerous thunderstorms, some of which become severe across the Piedmont and northern Coastal Plain and produced hail up to the size of golf balls and isolated wind damage.
episodes.158288: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northeast Georgia during the evening in advance of a cold front. One of these storms produced up to quarter size hail.
